text:
Jordan: heads up — after yesterday's kernel-routing change on canary we see a clear comm/compute overlap collapse on multi-GPU runs. throughput down ~12%, p99 token latency up ~30%. KV-cache warmups look delayed too. Posting quick trace and what I tried so far.

Hema: can you paste the trace + which commit/flags rolled out? any cudaGraph captures involved? :eyes:

Jordan: deployed commit `a3b9f4e` that adds heuristic to prefer the smaller-fused kernel for short sequences. This changes kernel affinity (different stream assignment). We do capture/replay graphs for the hot path.

Jordan: trace snippet (nvtx timestamped):
```
[GPU0] 0.001s stream=3 kernel=fast_fused_fp16 launch
[GPU0] 0.002s cudaGraphCaptureBegin gid=17
[GPU0] 0.003s stream=2 kernel=allreduce_cuda (waiting)
[GPU0] 0.004s hostSync() // surprising host sync inside capture
[GPU0] 0.005s cudaGraphCaptureEnd gid=17
[GPU0] 0.006s graphReplay(gid=17) -> stream3 enqueue
[GPU0] 0.0065s allreduce starts on stream0 but event wait on stream3 not signaled
[GPU0] 0.007s stall: compute blocked by comm handshake mismatch
```

Jordan: note the hostSync inside capture — that looks like the kernel we chose ended up doing a blocking host path (cudaEventSynchronize/host memcpy) which previously the old kernel path avoided. That breaks the expected stream ordering for the captured graph and disables overlap.

Ryan: that matches my hunch. The new fused kernel uses a host-side fallback for small batches (optimizes for latency) and emits a blocking `cudaMemcpyAsync` -> `cudaStreamSynchronize` in some paths. When that happens inside a capture region we end up serializing the capture and then the replay expects a different ordering.

Hema: can you repro with reduced config? e.g. force the heuristic to pick the previous kernel (env KERNEL_PICKER=legacy) and run the same trace? want to confirm it's kernel-selection policy, not an unrelated scheduling regression.

Jordan: did that — toggling back to legacy kernel immediately restores overlap and throughput. quick numbers:
``
legacy: throughput=1000 tok/s, p99=85ms
new-heuristic: throughput=880 tok/s, p99=110ms
``

Hema: okay good repro. We should either: 1) make the heuristic avoid host-blocking code paths when inside a cudaGraph capture OR 2) teach the capture logic to detect and fail fast (and skip capture) when a candidate kernel would insert host-syncs. Option 1 feels safer.

Ryan: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: make the batcher prefer the legacy kernel for sequences >1 and for pipeline-parallel segments that are captured. Also we need better unit tests in graph-mode to catch host-syncs.

Liz: can someone open an internal ticket with repro steps + the trace? add perf numbers and mark P1 for dedicated clusters. I'll coordinate a rollback if needed for dedicated.

Jordan: opened ISSUE-2026 with repro and attached trace + exact env flags. For immediate canary rollback I re-ran the deploy job with KERNEL_PICKER=legacy; canary metrics recovered within 10 minutes.

perf-bot: automated metric snapshot — before: throughput=1012 tok/s, after deploy: 885 tok/s, after rollback: 1008 tok/s.

Hema: follow-ups: (a) runtime: add a `capture-safe` flag to kernel descriptors (b) batcher: prefer capture-safe kernels when graph capture predicted (c) add a regression test that runs a short cudaGraph capture and asserts no host sync NVTX markers inside captures. I can take (a)+(c). Ryan take (b)?

Ryan: I'll take (b). Also will add an assertion in the graph replayer to detect unexpected host-syncs during replay and emit a clear warning so we can triage faster next time.

Jordan: thanks. tagging infra-bot to schedule a perf-run after the patches: @infra-bot canary perf job `kernel-graph-safety` please?

infra-bot: scheduled canary job `kernel-graph-safety` (job id 4281) — will post results when done.

Liz: thanks team. Let's keep the postmortem notes brief: root cause = kernel-selection heuristic picked a host-blocking micro-path incompatible with cudaGraph capture semantics, which serialized capture and destroyed comm/compute overlap. Mitigation = prefer capture-safe kernels and add tests + warning in replayer. :white_check_mark:

Jordan: I'll drop the nvprof output and small perf dashboard links into ISSUE-2026.

Ryan: one more note — this also explains KV-cache warmup delay: host-sync inside capture delays early KV-prefetch kernels, so prefix caching misses are hitting remote allreduce windows. worth adding to the issue.

Jordan: added that note. Closing the loop here, will post updates in the ticket. :thumbsup:
